steps: Find the decimal multiplier: increase → 1 + p/100, decrease → 1 − p/100
Compound change: multiply by multiplier raised to power n
Reverse percentage: divide by the multiplier
method_card.title: How to Work with Percentages & Compound Change
method_card.content:
To find a percentage of an amount: multiply by the percentage as a decimal. 15% of £80 = 0.15 × 80 = £12.

To increase by a percentage: multiply by \(1 + \frac{p}{100}\). A 20% increase uses multiplier 1.2.

To decrease by a percentage: multiply by \(1 - \frac{p}{100}\). A 15% decrease uses multiplier 0.85.

Compound change applies the multiplier repeatedly: after \(n\) years, amount = original \(\times\) multiplier\(^n\). This is used for interest, depreciation, and population growth.

To find the original amount after a percentage change (reverse percentage): divide by the multiplier instead of multiplying.
method_card.example:
£5000 is invested at 3% compound interest per year. Find the value after 4 years.

Multiplier = 1.03

Value = 5000 × 1.03⁴ = 5000 × 1.12550881 = £5627.54 (2 d.p.)

misconceptions.message: Interest per year = 5% of 2000 = 100. After 3 years = 3 × 100 = £300.

misconceptions.message: Reverse: divide by the multiplier. 96 ÷ 1.2 = £80. Don't subtract 20% of 96.
